query: Which material can be used for improve the magnetocaloric properties, and why?

generation.hypothesis: Refining the microstructure of Ni–Mn-based Heusler alloys through directional solidification or targeted heat treatments will enhance the magnetocaloric effect compared to conventional as-cast alloys.
generation.material_initial_state: Ni–Mn–X Heusler alloy in the as-cast condition
generation.intervention: Directional solidification or heat treatment to control grain size, phase distribution, and reduce lattice defects
generation.conditions: Processing above the alloy’s melting point followed by controlled cooling or annealing near the target magnetocaloric operating temperature
generation.structural_mediator: Refined grain boundaries and minimized structural defects to sharpen the magneto-structural transition
generation.mechanism: Reducing extrinsic disorder in the crystal lattice is expected to increase the magnetic entropy change and achieve a larger magnetocaloric response at the transition temperature
generation.predicted_outcome: A more pronounced and higher peak magnetocaloric effect near the desired working temperature relative to the as-cast baseline
generation.baseline: Unrefined, as-cast Ni–Mn–X Heusler alloys possessing broader transition widths and lower overall magnetocaloric output
generation.boundary: Exact magnitude of improvement will depend on alloy composition as well as specific processing temperatures, rates, and annealing profiles
generation.uncertainty: No direct quantitative data on magnetocaloric enhancement are found in the supplied sources, so the exact percentage gain is uncertain

falsification_experiment.design: Synthesize Ni–Mn–X Heusler alloy ingots and apply varying directional solidification or heat treatment protocols to produce different microstructural states, measuring their magnetocaloric response near the target temperature.
measurements: Magnetic entropy change (via magnetometry around the transition)
Microstructural characteristics by electron microscopy and diffraction
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the altered microstructure does not increase the magnetic entropy change (or if no sharpening of the magneto-structural transition is observed), then the hypothesis is refuted.

decision.unsolved: How to enhance the magnetocaloric effect for refrigeration applications remains unaddressed in the provided references. Achieving large entropy changes and tunable working temperatures without resorting to new alloying additions is still an open challenge.
decision.lever: Refining the microstructure of known magnetocaloric materials (e.g., Ni–Mn-based Heusler or La–Fe–Si compounds) through targeted heat treatments or directional solidification to optimize phase distribution and reduce defects, thereby enhancing the magnetocaloric response near the desired temperature range
decision.why: Adjusting phase proportions and grain structure can strengthen the magnetocaloric effect by sharpening or amplifying the magneto-structural transition, which directly addresses the question of achieving higher magnetocaloric performance without defaulting to additional alloy elements.
